chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Aban, from Mudrik ibn Abi Al-Hazhaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'I guarantee for the one who is moderate that he will not be impoverished.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material guarantee for practicing moderation in spending according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the spiritual discipline of moderation (*iqtisad*) directly to divine provision, promising that those who avoid excess and waste will be guaranteed sufficiency (*kifayah*) and freedom from poverty. This concept is central to Shia ethical teachings, where financial moderation is viewed not merely as economic prudence but as a means of preserving one's dignity and focus on worship, reflecting the broader Islamic principle that contentment is the true wealth.
